notes: Clatter (Brother Anselm Hobb, bible 5.9) in his mushroom garden among the Forgotten (the Ossuary, E26: placed in knot-outer, mw-3n0f; also reachable in the debug conversation room). Courteous, apologetic, tends pale mushrooms like a garden; the bones 'have opinions'. Memory stages follow the numeric fact clatter.memories (0 to 3 pieces of The Name on the Bones recovered, written by the quest): every stage has its own greeting and its own set of remembered fragments (ask-memory). If the song swells before he is restored the quest sets clatter.song-swelled and drops clatter.memories to 0: he notices something is missing (lost-1) and the dialogue clears the flag. While clatter.hostile (the Forgotten's fighting reflex has him, until the player hums the hymn or lowers a weapon) he only apologises (barks). Once clatter.restored he asks to rest or to join; either is right (bible 6.1). Class branches: sorcerer reads his memories (a gamble: success skips a piece, failure costs one, once only), thief returns a thing he does not know he lost, knight stands guard (and gives the rites if he asks for rest), archer keeps watch. Not placed yet: the Ossuary scenes belong to E26. mw-e39.11 (The Name on the Bones): meeting him sets clatter.met (starts the quest). Three pieces are handed to him here, each its own hub option: the psalter (evidence.clatter-psalter), the blooming pear tree (bones.pear-bloomed, Juniper) and the letter from the Pell Bible (hollis.bible-lent); each sets its bones.*-given fact and moves clatter.memories up one through `bump`. When memories reach clatter.memories.max (3, or 2 after a failed reading), the name moment plays, and the quest sets clatter.restored. A failed sorcerer reading drops clatter.memories.max to 2 for good (read-lost) as well as costing the memory he held; a successful one sets clatter.read-success. The knight's rites set clatter.rites.

nodes.speaker: clatter
nodes.text: Sorry! Sorry. I don't want to hit you, it's the bones, they have opinions. Please stand somewhere I'm not aiming. Further. A bit further. Thank you, sorry.

nodes.speaker: clatter
nodes.text: Oh, you again. Sorry, sorry, the arm is doing it. I'm not doing it. I'd like that noted, if anyone is noting.

options.text: Lower your weapon and wait.
Hum the Vesper hymn, softly.
Back away slowly.

nodes.speaker: clatter
nodes.text: Oh. Oh, that's very decent of you. The arm has stopped, look. It's thinking about it. Sorry, it's still thinking about it.

nodes.speaker: clatter
nodes.text: Oh. Oh, that's the evening one. Somebody used to... Sorry, I've gone quiet all through, right down to the knees. That is a lovely tune, as long as it stays small.

nodes.speaker: clatter
nodes.text: Thank you! Thank you, I'll try not to follow. The legs have opinions as well, I'm afraid. Sorry. Sorry! Mind the mushrooms!

nodes.speaker: clatter
nodes.text: I had something just now. It was round. A pear? No, it's gone. It was in my hands and it's gone. Was someone humming? I think someone was humming.

nodes.speaker: clatter
nodes.text: Sorry. It's only that I'd got so far. I'd laid it all out like seedlings, and then the whole tray went. Never mind. We start again. Gardeners are good at starting again.

nodes.speaker: clatter
nodes.text: Oh! Oh, hello. Sorry, I wasn't... Do mind the mushrooms, they're easily offended. I'd offer you a seat, but I can't remember where I put the chairs. Or whether there were chairs.

nodes.speaker: clatter
nodes.text: The goblins call me Clatter. I assume that's because of the clatter. I can't think what else it would be for.

nodes.speaker: clatter
nodes.text: Hello again. Sorry. I do know you, I think; I know your feet. Mind the mushrooms. They've started sulking. I can't think what I did.

nodes.speaker: clatter
nodes.text: Ah, hello. I've got a pear tree now. Just the one. I keep it in my head, between the fourth and fifth thoughts, and I water it twice a day. It's very good company.

nodes.speaker: clatter
nodes.text: Hello! I had a sister. And a tree. I'm so full of things I've had to start a second pocket. Sorry, I'm talking too much. Do stop me. Or don't. It's rather nice.

nodes.speaker: clatter
nodes.text: Hello, friend. I nearly have it. My name's on the tip of my tongue, if I had a tongue. Sorry. Nearly. Do you ever feel that someone is about to say a word that's yours?

options.text: I found a psalter among the Forgotten. 'A. Hobb' on the flyleaf.
The dead pear tree in the priory garden has bloomed.
I have a letter. A Brother Anselm, to his sister. From the Pell family Bible.
What do you remember?
Tell me about the mushrooms.
The goblins call you Clatter?
You look afraid. What of?
May I try to read your memories? It might hurt.
I found this by the Ossuary door. Yours?
I'll stand watch at the door while you work.
I can keep the Forgotten off your garden from the stair.
Goodbye, Clatter.

nodes.speaker: clatter
nodes.text: Mushrooms. I remember mushrooms. And that I'm sorry, though I don't know what for. I think it was a large sorry, the kind you carry up a staircase.

nodes.speaker: clatter
nodes.text: There's a gap where a name goes. Rather a tidy gap. I've been keeping it dusted.

nodes.speaker: clatter
nodes.text: A pear tree. There was a pear tree, white in spring, and the bees went at it like a rumour. I used to stand under it and do nothing at all. Nobody told me off.

nodes.speaker: clatter
nodes.text: I can't see whose garden it was. But I can smell it. Isn't that odd? A bone, smelling a pear.

nodes.speaker: clatter
nodes.text: A sister. She laughed like a gate that wanted oiling. I... liked that gate. She sent me letters in a hand like a hen's. I can see the hen. I can't see the name.

nodes.speaker: clatter
nodes.text: There was a friend, too. Taller than me. Afraid of the quiet. I think he was the only person I ever knew who kept a candle lit to hear it burn.

nodes.speaker: clatter
nodes.text: Corvin. He was afraid of silence, which is why he fell so hard for a song. I could have told him. I think I did tell him. It's the sort of thing a gardener says to a friend, over a fence.

nodes.speaker: clatter
nodes.text: And my sister's grandchildren, a long way down the line. A baker, I think. I can smell the bread. Anselm... Anselm Ho... No. Sorry. Nearly. The rest is loose in the soil.

nodes.speaker: clatter
nodes.text: Pale ones, mostly. They don't mind the dark, and I don't mind them, which is the whole arrangement. I turn them over, I tell them they're doing well. I'm told it helps.

nodes.speaker: clatter
nodes.text: The goblins say it's a flower room. I haven't the heart to correct them.

nodes.speaker: clatter
nodes.text: A little one brings me buttons, and tells me what they're for. Snig, I think. Always wrong, always enthusiastic. I keep the buttons in the soil. They haven't come up yet, but one has hope.

nodes.speaker: clatter
nodes.text: Mother Kettleback sends bread, because I look peckish. I tell her I haven't the equipment. She sends it anyway. Goblins are very kind in a way that doesn't ask what you meant.

nodes.speaker: clatter
nodes.text: The humming. When it swells, I go loose. Whatever I've gathered goes down the drain, and I stand there, a bag of bones in a good habit, wondering where I put myself.

nodes.speaker: clatter
nodes.text: So if you hear it coming, do stand close. Not for me, necessarily. Someone ought to be there to say, 'Brother, you were just in the middle of something.'

nodes.speaker: clatter
nodes.text: A trowel! A little trowel, with a handle gone soft as a pear. Oh, it is. It's mine. I didn't know I'd lost it. How did you know?

nodes.speaker: clatter
nodes.text: You have a gift. I hope you use it on the rich. Thank you. Truly.

nodes.speaker: clatter
nodes.text: Oh, thank you. A knight at the door! The Forgotten will like that, they love a uniform. Only don't hit them too hard. Most of them were someone's uncle.

nodes.speaker: clatter
nodes.text: You'd hit a snail at forty paces? Sorry, that's what Snig says. He says it about you. I think he made it up. Still, I'll sleep easier. If I slept. Which I don't. But I would.

nodes.speaker: clatter
nodes.text: Oh. Yes. Go on. It may sting? Sorry. I mean I'm sorry if it stings you. It won't me. I haven't the nerve.

nodes.speaker: clatter
nodes.text: ...Oh! Oh, there's a drawer. I didn't know there was a drawer! Thank you. There's so much in the drawer.

nodes.speaker: clatter
nodes.text: Ah. Ow. Not you, me. Something went, with a noise like a spoon in a drain. It's all right. It's quite all right. I'm sure it was a good one.

nodes.speaker: clatter
nodes.text: Goodbye! Mind the mushrooms. And mind the bones, they have opinions about your knees.

nodes.speaker: clatter
nodes.text: I'm right behind you. Or beside. Beside's better, I trip over things behind. Sorry. Lead on, friend. Is it a long walk? I do hope it's a long walk.

options.text: Tell me about your sister again.
Right. Onward.

nodes.speaker: clatter
nodes.text: Her name was Amabel. Amabel Hobb. She laughed like a gate. I'd give a good deal of my bones to hear that gate again. Tansy has the laugh, did you notice? Quite uncanny. Sorry. Not uncanny. Lovely.

nodes.speaker: clatter
nodes.text: Brother Anselm Hobb. Gardener. Friend of Corvin Ashgrove, and sorry for it. Sorry. Is it all right to say it aloud? I like the sound of it. It's got shoulders.

nodes.speaker: clatter
nodes.text: I've a question and I'd rather you didn't answer fast. I've been dead a long while and it's gone to my head. Is it time to rest? Or is there something yet for hands like mine to do?

options.text: Say it again.
Come with me to the Cradle. Corvin should hear his friend.
You've done enough. Would you like to rest?
Take your time, Anselm. I'm in no hurry.

nodes.speaker: clatter
nodes.text: Anselm Hobb. Anselm Hobb! Oh, I'd forgotten how good that was. It has a tidy sound. Like a gate closing. A well-oiled one.

nodes.speaker: clatter
nodes.text: Yes. Yes, I think so. I've something to say to him. Not an argument. A gardener's remark, over a fence. Give me a moment. I'll find my feet. They're just here.

nodes.speaker: clatter
nodes.text: Oh, would you? The old words? The Vesperine rites? I'd have been so embarrassed to ask. I've been hoping someone knew them. Lay down the bell, lay down the work... Yes. Yes, that's the one.

nodes.speaker: clatter
nodes.text: Thank you, Sir Knight. It's a very good voice for it. Rather a lot like a gate, actually.

nodes.speaker: clatter
nodes.text: Yes. I think I would. Lay my psalter on the altar, if you'd be so kind. Water the pear tree if it blooms. And tell Tansy her great-great-great-aunt's gate is still oiled. She'll know.

nodes.speaker: clatter
nodes.text: Oh. Oh, that's. The gnaw is Mortimer's, no, that's not right, Mortimer's a cat, I don't. That's my hand. That's my writing. A. H. Hobb. His. 'Do not lend.' I wrote that. I wrote it for Corvin. He was very bad about giving things back.

nodes.speaker: clatter
nodes.text: Corvin. There's a Corvin. I had a friend and he was afraid of the quiet. Oh, dear. Thank you. I'd have been very upset to find that out later.

nodes.speaker: clatter
nodes.text: Bloomed? Truly? The one by the wall, with the crooked branch like an elbow? Did it smell? Pears smell of... of rain and sugar and a little of the barn.

nodes.speaker: clatter
nodes.text: I used to talk to it. Not to be silly. It's only that someone had to. It never answered, but it kept every word, I think, the way a tree keeps weather. Thank you. Thank you for the tree.

nodes.speaker: clatter
nodes.text: A letter. To my sister? She had a... She laughed like a gate. 'Dear Amabel. I am well. The priory is cold, and I have found a man here who is afraid of silence, and I am teaching him to like gardens.' ...Oh. That's me. That's me, isn't it?

nodes.speaker: clatter
nodes.text: 'Tell Hollis's grandmother the pears are for her.' I know a Hollis. Hollis's gran, with the sharp elbows. We've the same elbows, her and I. Amabel. Amabel Hobb. Thank you for bringing her. I'm so sorry I forgot her.

nodes.speaker: clatter
nodes.text: ...Anselm. Anselm Hobb. Brother Anselm Hobb, who tended the pears. Oh. Oh, it fits. It fits like a glove, if I had hands to... I have hands. Look! I have my name!

nodes.speaker: clatter
nodes.text: Sorry. Sorry. Give me a moment. I've a great deal to be sorry for and a great deal more to be glad of, and they've started in at once. Come and find me when I've sat down.
